verdict.rationale: Stripe exposes programmatic building blocks relevant to an agent workflow — a Value Lists API for managing blocklists/allowlists (stripe-radar-docs-10, stripe-radar-docs-14) and a Reviews API with an explicit approve endpoint that maps naturally to a human-approval gate (stripe-radar-docs-8, stripe-radar-docs-21) — plus a documented official MCP server (stripe-radar-probe-4) that could let an agent call these APIs. However, Radar rules (e.g. a velocity rule) are documented only as Dashboard-configurable via a rules reference of supported attributes (stripe-radar-docs-3), with no evidenced API endpoint for programmatically proposing/creating rules, and community commentary explicitly flags a lack of easy programmatic control over Radar decisions (stripe-radar-comm-2) and notes allow-rule changes require contacting support rather than self-serve API access (stripe-radar-comm-7). Missing for 10: a documented rules-creation/update API endpoint, evidence the MCP server actually surfaces rule/list-management tools, and confirmation that approval gating is agent-triggerable rather than dashboard-only.
